Name: Martin J Pitt
Question: Would an adult from 2022 be able to go back to say 1955 and blend in?
Answer: With one reservation, I’m sure I could. I was 7 then. Rationing of food had just ended, which removes one difficulty. I could work with pre-decimal money, understand the postal system, manage buses with conductors, drink tea with sterilised milk (because it lasts longer if you don’t have a fridge) and have a daily pinta of full-cream milk from the milkman for our morning Weetabix and cooking. I’d be happy with white bread from the co-op with margarine, luncheon meat, beans on toast, herring roes as a treat, and fish and chips at least once a week. I can use an old-fashioned tin-opener. I could lay a coal fire, though I hope we’d have coke (and would appreciate the Clean Air Act next year) and cook on coal gas. I could wash clothes in a boiler, though a washing machine would be nice, then use a mangle and hang them on a line. I would find it hard to deal with the tobacco smoke everywhere. Walls and skirting boards were painted white but quickly became cream. My biggest difficulty would be explaining what I had been doing in two World Wars in order to earn my state pension.

Question: Hi. I plan to study in UK for my bachelors study in computer science. Does anyone know any decent universities that are normally commutable from Reading (post code RG1), for up to 1 hour of travel by public transport like busses and trains?
Answer: I guess you have some friends or relations in Reading who have agreed to give you accommodation, That is certainly helpful. I would describe the University of Reading as a decent university. It has been a university for nearly a hundred years, and was a university college before then. Here is the link for Computer Science: You will need to apply through the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (UCAS) Note that you can apply to up to 5 universities, but you don’t have to. You can apply to only one. This simplifies matters for the Admissions Tutor, and probably you. If they reject you, I guess you won’t want to look at more distant places. For entry in September 2023, the deadline for applications is 15 January. However, after this UCAS will still pass on your form. Departments tend to give more allowance to late applications by students from other countries. (The fact that the course fees are considerably higher than for home students may be a factor.) If it is difficult for you to manage an application by this time, I recommend you email the department to ask if you will be considered.

Question: How is the origin of sexual reproduction explained in the context of evolution? The ability to reproduce sexually isn't useful until at least 2 people can do it, and it's unlikely that two people would develop the trait at the same time (and place).
Answer: It didn’t start with people, it started with micro-organisms more than a billion years ago. Essentially it was a fault in mitosis: the process by which a cell divides by replicating its DNA so that two cells with identical genes are reproduced. The fault meant that the splitting only produced cells with half the DNA, but if two of these met, they could provide a viable organism, often with a different selection of genes. This produced mixing of genes which enabled a greater rate of evolution. Initially there were no males and females, just half-DNA cells called gametes floating about. However, through random changes some became larger, some smaller, and this is how sex is essentially defined. The female is the larger gamete, the male the smaller one. In the most primitive cases, the difference is small, but has an effect. The female can contain more material to get the new joined cell going, the male can spread more easily. Add hundreds of millions of years and we have lots of specializations such as in flowers and mammals where the male and female gametes are very different, and processes to get them together are extremely complex and varied,
